novelty_flags.label: thm:anytime-qte-coverage
novelty_flags.one_line: MineiroHoward2023 already proves time- and value-uniform importance-weighted counterfactual-CDF bands for a changing historical target, which specializes to each fixed-potential-outcome arm and gives QTE coverage by deterministic inverse-CDF subtraction.

novelty_flags.label: thm:anytime-qte-coverage

soundness_flags.label: def:anytime-band-class and thm:functional-lil-lower-bound
soundness_flags.one_line: The band class imposes coverage but no requirement that each C_t be measurable with respect to observed data F_t; it therefore admits the oracle singleton band C_t(q)={tau_t(q)}, making the asserted positive width lower bound untenable.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1-2, Eq. (1)-(2) and contributions; p. 5, Section 3.4 and Theorem 3.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper targets an evolving historical conditional CDF, proves simultaneous time- and value-uniform bands, and extends them to importance-weighted counterfactual distributions.
The paper gives i.i.d. quantile confidence sequences uniform in time and, for its all-quantile construction, uniform in quantile, at a square-root log-log rate.
The paper proposes covariate-adjusted response-adaptive QTE designs and states that its QTE estimator attains a semiparametric optimal variance lower bound.
The paper studies design-based finite-population ATE Neyman regret, with anytime near-logarithmic noncontextual regret and multigroup guarantees.
Clip-OGD studies design-based adaptive Neyman allocation, defines Neyman regret, obtains expected tilde-O(sqrt(T)) regret, and supplies a conservative variance estimator for ATE inference.
The paper establishes compact-quantile-index weak limits for simple and IPW QTE estimators under covariate-adaptive randomization and develops bootstrap inference.
The paper formulates a minimax multi-objective Pareto trade-off between welfare regret and treatment-effect inference and gives Pareto-optimal adaptive experiments.

The paper concerns sequential adaptive ATE inference, including nonasymptotic and asymptotic confidence sequences under changing assignment policies; its actual venue is CLeaR, not AISTATS as stated in the bibliography.
The paper develops inference for adaptively collected experimental data using adaptively weighted augmented inverse-propensity methods.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make membership in the anytime-band class explicitly require F_t-measurable, observed-data-only endpoints (including any auxiliary randomization), then restate the lower bound over that restricted class.
Remove the root regret-width identity or replace it with a substantive attainability/strict-gap theorem; retaining a definition rearrangement as a solve target makes the current artifact vacuous.

Reframe the explicit coverage result as a specialization, simplification, or sharper finite-population calibration of MineiroHoward2023 and WaudbySmithWuRamdasKarampatziakisMineiro2022, with a stated strict advantage over their constructions.

Keep Phi as the focal field-level object, but specify a tractable restricted design family or a worked nonconstant two-quantile instance on which its frontier is computed; this makes the proposed saddle construction empirically and mathematically discriminating.

recommended_next_step: Revise this angle: restrict bands to observed-data procedures, delete or strengthen the definitional proposition, and reposition the coverage construction against the existing off-policy CDF-band literature before advancing to Stage 0.
